rejected.title: Growth of tourism
card: Tourism is travel away from home for leisure, visiting people or other purposes. It is now one of the largest industries in the world.
Cheaper flights
Larger planes and more competition between airlines have lowered fares, so more people can afford to travel far.
Higher incomes
As incomes rise, more families have money left over after paying for basics. Some of it can be spent on holidays.
The internet
People can compare prices, book flights and rooms, and read reviews online. This makes trips easier to plan and book.
rejected.remember: Tourism has grown because travel costs less, people have more money and planning is easy.

a.q: Leila in Hobart uses her phone to compare hotel prices and read reviews of resorts in Bali. Which cause of tourism growth does this show?
opts: The internet, which makes trips easier to plan
Cheaper flights, which make long trips affordable
Higher incomes, which leave money for holidays
Larger planes, which carry more people per flight
a.why: Comparing prices and reading reviews on a phone is using the internet to plan a trip. Cheaper flights lower the cost of travel, but they do not explain how Leila researches her holiday.
a.clue: Is Leila paying less, earning more, or planning in a new way?

b.q: Two airlines start flying the same route from Adelaide to Bali and compete for passengers. How is this most likely to add to tourism?
opts: Lower fares, so more people can afford to fly
Higher incomes, so families have more to spend
More online reviews, so trips are easier to plan
Higher fares, so airlines can buy larger planes
b.why: Airlines that compete for passengers tend to cut fares, so more people can afford the trip. Competition does not raise anyone's income: higher incomes are a separate cause of tourism growth.
b.clue: Think about what airlines do to win customers from each other.

flags: Remember, wording: The remember line says 'planning is easy', but the card says the internet makes trips 'easier to plan'. 'Easier to plan' would match the card.

a.q: Which change has made it easier for people to book trips without a travel agent?
opts: Booking flights and rooms online
Larger planes on long routes
Rising household incomes
More competition between airlines
a.why: Online booking lets people compare prices and reserve trips themselves. Cheaper fares come from planes and competition, which lower cost but do not change how people book.
a.clue: Think about where people now search and book.

b.q: Priya's family in Perth could not afford overseas holidays 20 years ago. Now they take one each year. Which change best explains this on its own?
opts: Their income has risen, leaving more money to spend
Airlines have stopped competing on ticket prices
Fewer people now use the internet to plan trips
Travel away from home has become less popular
b.why: Higher income leaves spare money after paying for basics, so a holiday becomes affordable. Less competition would raise fares, which would make travel harder, not easier.
b.clue: Look for the change that gives a family more money to spend.

b.best: Their income has risen, leaving more money to spend
